rationale: Observed uncertainty: candidate 374e89a7 (parent 46bcc1f2 + additive bundle trial-2ffc01d1ba, route stem_microbatch_rows8) measured peak_allocated_bytes 177409024, exactly equal to its paired parent reference, with decision reasons paired_gain_not_above_noise and objective_not_improved, while quality passed and the throughput constraint held. Coverage shows the declared stem route with only 2 candidate invocations versus 32 reference invocations for that bundle (16 for the parent's stage0 bundle), and the endpoint interpretation explicitly warns that route labels are candidate-reported telemetry, not native proof, to be corroborated with traces or actual exception evidence. Two questions follow: (1) does the added stem-microbatch route actually execute its microbatched path, or is it bypassed via handled exceptions or False guards falling back to the reference stem (which would explain the bit-identical objective); (2) if it does execute, does the trace show the expected rows8 launch pattern and any serialization/overlap with the parent bundle's stage0 microbatches that bears on remaining peak reduction. Selections: candidate_diagnostics records exceptions (including handled ones with library traceback locations) and False returns in the supplied candidate files on this exact revision - the only source of actual exception evidence for silent fallback; its known limit is that empty events do not establish which successful path executed, so nsys is selected to corroborate with trace evidence: per-kernel launch timeline with grid/block dimensions and CUDA API submissions, showing independently of candidate labels whether stem convolutions launch microbatched (4x rows8-sized grids vs one rows32 grid) and how kernels serialize or overlap within one measured invocation. nsys is available (request.json tools.nsys). Exclusions: torch already ran; nccl_tuning/collective_calibration are inapplicable (single device, no NCCL per observations.json); device_telemetry cannot attribute allocator peaks; execution_timeline is redundant for attribution since torch already associated 157/157 kernels with zero ambiguity and its comm-oriented bounds add nothing; python_runtime and binding_cost address host dispatch and binding overhead, neither implicated by the observed memory-objective uncertainty. No failure-category policy or optimization action is presumed; the residual peak's per-stage ownership stays listed as unavailable because no collector supplies per-group allocator attribution.
